attendees.role: vice chair, addressed throughout as Richard

minutes.headline: Commission passed a motion letting one member keep managing trust funds if it loses quorum
minutes.summary: The trust fund commission's chair delivered an extended legal presentation arguing the town, select board, town manager and school department are in breach of fiduciary duty under Massachusetts trust law (MGL 203E) for decades of undistributed trust income, and reported an attorney general breach notice has been filed and is under review. The commission then voted to adopt a formal motion preserving fiduciary oversight and authorizing a lone remaining commissioner to continue ministerial/administrative duties if the board loses quorum; no trust money was distributed at this meeting.

votes.motion: That the board of commissioners of trust funds, acting under its authority under MGL chapter 41 sections 45-47 and its fiduciary obligations under the Massachusetts Uniform Trust Code (MGL 203E), adopt the comprehensive motion and statement of findings on continuation of fiduciary oversight and delegation of authority upon loss of a quorum

The chair noted the cemetery commission did not put a request for a sum on this year's town meeting warrant after he clarified the cemetery commission is its own trustee body with independent authority to use its own funds.

budget_items.what_was_said: Richard read a statement prepared with other residents arguing the town's balanced budget maintains core operations without an override, that tier one appears to be the intended landing point, and that no department has shown the override is legally necessary.

what_happened.line: Commission voted unanimously to let one remaining commissioner keep handling administrative trust duties if the board loses quorum.
Chair said trust fund interest has gone undistributed to veterans, the poor and other purposes for over 50 years, and read a legal memo arguing the town is in breach of state trust law.
Chair reported the Attorney General's office has received and is reviewing the commission's breach notice against the town.
A commissioner read prepared remarks arguing no department has shown the proposed override is legally necessary.

why_it_matters: This is a fiduciary-oversight and governance question about who controls disbursement of long-held trust income for veterans, the poor, sidewalks and similar town purposes -- not a vote to release any money now.

A pending Attorney General review of an alleged breach of trust law involving the town, select board, town manager and school department could affect how the town is required to handle these funds going forward.
The prepared remarks against the FY27 override, read at this meeting, feed into the town's ongoing override debate ahead of town meeting.
